subject: Critical velocity watch: evaluation handoff & MAP update
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@whitespace.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close timeline — early concern on evaluation window

Jonas,

Quick note from our side — the pilot evaluation window that we planned for mid-July is getting squeezed on the partner side. Two things changing: (1) our engineering lead has a parallel blackout the week of Jul 20 and (2) the procurement gate at Acme has moved their final review to Aug 2. Those shifts mean we may not hit the original Aug 1 go-live without compressing the MAP.

Can you share a compact plan that shows: 1) what minimal evaluation criteria we must meet to keep the original commitment, and 2) a recommended re-baseline (dates + single-point owners) if we need to slip by ~3 weeks? If Redwood can offer an interim staging arrangement or a limited-capacity pilot earlier that might help the procurement narrative.

Appreciate a short options list we can review with Acme procurement tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sarah
-- 
Sarah Lim
Head of Platform Integrations, Acme Corp
sarah.lim@acme.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close timeline — early concern on evaluation window

Sarah — thanks for flagging this early. Short reply with an attached compact MAP (MAP_v2.pdf) and a proposed 2‑lane plan: lane A preserves the original Aug 1 target by narrowing eval acceptance to a core 6 tests (perf p95, 1 critical regression, security smoke, integration sanity, basic accuracy slice, infra resilience). That requires Acme to commit 2 dedicated engineer-days/week for three weeks.

Lane B is a conservative re-baseline that moves go-live to Aug 22 but gives you a formal handoff: Redwood runs a 1-week assisted eval (we staff an SRE + Solutions Engineer) and delivers a signed evaluation runbook and regression checklist. This lane removes the need for Acme's engineering blackout to block the decision.

Key asks from your side for either lane: a single evaluation owner, confirmation of the SOC2 evidence acceptance (we attached SOC2_snippet.pdf), and a procurement contact for the DocuSign/PO timeline. If you confirm by EOD Wed we can lock resource availability.

Attachments: MAP_v2.pdf, SOC2_snippet.pdf

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close timeline — early concern on evaluation window

Looping in a quick operational option set. If Acme prefers to keep Aug 1 as the customer-visible target but cannot provide engineering time, we can propose an "assisted-limited" pilot: Redwood provides an internal-only pilot environment for 10 days where we run the key acceptance tests against a redacted dataset. That reduces Acme lift but requires an abbreviated SOW amendment and a one-week surge from our Solutions Engineering pool.

Practical notes: 1) I can allocate one SE for the assisted pilot for the week of Jul 13 (need notice by Jun 17), 2) procurement: we can issue a conditional invoice for the surge to expedite the PO, and 3) runbook: see the attached eval-runbook.xlsx — it lists pass/fail criteria and the single-point owners we should agree on.

If Acme is comfortable with the Aug 22 re-baseline, we should still sign a short interim agreement that locks the rollout cadence and assigns rollout owners to avoid another slip. Suggest a 30-minute executive alignment call Fri 6/12 — please propose a time.

Attachments: eval-runbook.xlsx

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@whitespace.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close timeline — critical velocity watch: evaluation handoff & MAP update

Marissa, Jonas — thank you, this is helpful and concrete. We spoke briefly with procurement; they prefer the Aug 22 re-baseline but will accept the assisted-limited pilot if Redwood can limit surge exposure and provide an acceptance-attestation doc for the redacted run. Two actionable items from Acme: (1) I will confirm our single evaluation owner (you should expect an email from Jeff Walker by EOD Fri 6/12), and (2) procurement asks for the conditional invoice language you mentioned — can you share a one-page amendment template we can circulate?

We are available for the executive check-in Friday 6/12 at 10:00am PT if that works for your team. If so, please send a calendar invite and a short agenda (15 minutes).

Thanks —
Sarah
Sarah Lim
Head of Platform Integrations, Acme Corp
